item.title: Jamaica: IOM Hurricane Melissa Situation Report #19
item.description:
Country: Jamaica
Source: International Organization for Migration

Please refer to the attached file.

Jamaica: IOM Hurricane Melissa Response Situation Report No. 19 (Reporting Period: November 2025 – September 2026)

Nearly one year after Hurricane Melissa impacted Jamaica, IOM continues to support recovery and resilience-building efforts in the country’s most affected communities. This 19th Situation Report outlines progress across shelter rehabilitation, emergency shelter upgrades, non-food item (NFI) assistance, livelihoods support, and psychosocial services delivered in partnership with the Government of Jamaica, local authorities, implementing partners, and affected communities.

Key achievements include shelter repair support reaching 3,989 households, including both light and heavy repairs, alongside Build Back Safer initiatives that have reached approximately 21,000 households through awareness-raising and technical guidance. IOM has also advanced improvements to community centres identified as potential emergency shelters, strengthening preparedness and protection capacities ahead of future hurricane seasons.

During the reporting period, IOM finalized its NFI distribution activities, providing essential household items to vulnerable hurricane-affected families and bringing total beneficiaries of NFI assistance to more than 31,200 individuals. Debris removal and Cash-for-Work interventions have concluded, benefiting 5,928 people while helping restore access to critical infrastructure and supporting local economic recovery. Psychological First Aid activities also concluded after reaching more than 1,000 individuals and training 104 community focal points and volunteers.

Looking ahead, IOM will continue expanding shelter repair assistance, complete upgrades to remaining community shelters, strengthen joint initiatives with UN partners, and undertake post-intervention monitoring to assess impact and inform future preparedness and recovery efforts. The report highlights the importance of sustained partnerships and investment in resilience to help communities better withstand future disasters.

item.title: Mexico: Latinoamérica y El Caribe Resumen de Situación Semanal al 23 de octubre 2026
item.description:
Countries: Mexico, El Salvador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Panama
Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Please refer to the attached Infographic.

CIFRAS CLAVE

  • 20K personas desplazadas en el último mes en Haití debido a la violencia
  • 5K personas permanecen en albergues tras un terremoto de magnitud 7,5 en Panamá
  • 183K personas podrían enfrentar inseguridad alimentaria de nivel de crisis en el Corredor Seco

MÉXICO: HURACANES

Otra tormenta se está formando frente a la costa pacífica de México, que aún se está recuperando de una serie de huracanes esta temporada. Vance se ha fortalecido hasta convertirse en huracán a primera hora del 23 de octubre, y el Centro Nacional de Huracanes de EE. UU. (NOAA) prevé que se intensifique rápidamente hasta convertirse en un huracán mayor. Los meteorólogos esperan que permanezca en el mar, moviéndose paralelo a la costa, pero advierten que sigue siendo posible un giro hacia la costa centro-oeste. Incluso en alta mar, se prevé que sus bandas exteriores traerán fuertes lluvias a la costa de Guerrero y al centro y suroeste de Michoacán, donde sucesivas tormentas ya han saturado el terreno. El huracán Trudy también permaneció frente a la costa la semana pasada, aunque aun así trajo fuertes lluvias e inundaciones al estado de Colima, incluyendo Manzanillo, Villa de Álvarez y la capital del estado, Colima. Impulsada por El Niño, esta se ha convertido en la temporada de huracanes más activa registrada en el este y centro del Pacífico. Vance es la vigésima tercera tormenta nombrada en ambas cuencas, en comparación con las aproximadamente 15 de una temporada promedio.

HAITÍ: DESPLAZAMIENTO

La violencia armada sigue obligando a las personas a abandonar sus hogares a medida que se extiende más allá de Puerto Príncipe. Según la Matriz de Seguimiento del Desplazamiento de la OIM, casi el 80% de los casi 1,5 millones de personas desplazadas en Haití viven ahora fuera de la capital. El 18 de octubre, la violencia en el municipio de Arcahaie, al norte de Puerto Príncipe en el departamento de Ouest, obligó a casi 2.900 personas a huir. En Petite Rivière de l'Artibonite, los ataques desde el 19 de octubre han desplazado a unas 7.250 personas más. Junto con los ataques de finales de septiembre en Gros Morne, que desplazaron a más de 10.000 personas, estos eventos han desplazado a más de 20.000 personas en menos de un mes. La mayoría ha encontrado refugio con familias de acogida en lugar de en campamentos, lo que supone una gran carga para las comunidades, que cuentan con recursos propios limitados.

PANAMÁ: TERREMOTO

Las fuertes lluvias están generando nuevos riesgos mientras continúa la respuesta al terremoto de magnitud 7,5 del 9 de octubre. El 20 de octubre, el Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil de Panamá (SINAPROC) puso en alerta amarilla los distritos de Soná y Mariato, en la provincia de Veraguas, y el distrito de Tonosí, en la provincia de Los Santos, debido a las fuertes lluvias. Las lluvias ya han provocado deslizamientos de tierra en las carreteras de Los Santos, amenazando a poblaciones ya vulnerables, incluidas familias desplazadas que siguen necesitando albergue y servicios básicos. Al 20 de octubre, unas 5.000 personas permanecen en 126 albergues temporales, principalmente en Veraguas, mientras que otras siguen durmiendo en tiendas de campaña por temor a las réplicas. El terremoto ha afectado a más de 35.000 personas y ha dañado más de 9.000 viviendas, y las escuelas de Los Santos, Herrera, Coclé y Veraguas siguen cerradas. Las autoridades de salud están monitoreando 908 casos respiratorios y 473 casos entéricos, ya que la lluvia aumenta el riesgo de brotes de enfermedades.

CENTROAMÉRICA: INSEGURIDAD ALIMENTARIA

El Niño está profundizando el hambre en el Corredor Seco de Centroamérica, donde la sequía prolongada ha dejado a las familias agricultoras con cosechas perdidas y reservas de alimentos cada vez más escasas. En la región fronteriza del Trifinio, compartida por El Salvador, Guatemala y Honduras, algunas zonas han pasado hasta 75 días sin lluvia. La sequía ha destruido gran parte de la cosecha de maíz y frijol de la Primera, de la que dependen los hogares para reponer sus reservas de granos. El aumento de los costos se suma a las pérdidas; los precios del diésel en Guatemala casi se duplicaron entre enero y septiembre. Un análisis actualizado de la Clasificación Integrada de las Fases de la Seguridad Alimentaria (CIF) proyecta ahora que 183.000 personas enfrentarán una Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) o peor entre noviembre y marzo de 2027, más del doble de la previsión anterior. La microregión de Ch'orti' y Ocotepeque en Honduras son las más afectadas.

item.title: Mexico: Latin America & The Caribbean Weekly Situation Update as of 23 October 2026
item.description:
Countries: Mexico, El Salvador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Panama
Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Please refer to the attached Infographic.

KEY FIGURES

  • 20K people displaced in the last month across Haiti due to violence
  • 5K people remain in shelters after a 7.5 earthquake in Panama
  • 183K people projected to face Crisis-level food insecurity in the Dry Corridor

MEXICO: HURRICANES

Another storm is building off Mexico’s Pacific coast, which is still recovering from a run of hurricanes this season. Vance strengthened into a hurricane early on 23 October, and the US National Hurricane Center (NOAA) expects it to intensify rapidly into a major hurricane. Forecasters expect it to stay at sea, moving parallel to the coastline, but warn that a turn toward the west-central coast remains possible. Even offshore, its outer bands are forecast to bring heavy rain to coastal Guerrero and central and south-west Michoacán, where successive storms have already saturated the ground. Hurricane Trudy also stayed offshore last week, yet it still brought heavy rain and flooding to Colima state, including Manzanillo, Villa de Álvarez and the state capital, Colima. Fuelled by El Niño, this has become the most active eastern and central Pacific Hurricane season on record. Vance is the 23rd named storm across the two basins, compared with about 15 in an average season.

HAITI: DISPLACEMENT

Armed violence continues to drive people from their homes as it spreads beyond Port-au-Prince. According to IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix, nearly 80 per cent of Haiti’s almost 1.5 million displaced people now live outside the capital. On 18 October, violence in the Arcahaie municipality, north of Port-au-Prince in Ouest department, forced nearly 2,900 people to flee. In Petite Rivière de l’Artibonite, attacks since 19 October have displaced some 7,250 more. Together with the late-September attacks in Gros Morne, which displaced more than 10,000 people, these events have displaced more than 20,000 people in less than a month. Most have found refuge with host families rather than in sites, placing heavy demands on communities with limited resources of their own.

PANAMA: EARTHQUAKE

Heavy rain is creating new risks as the response to the 9 October magnitude 7.5 earthquake continues. On 20 October, Panama’s National Civil Protection System (SINAPROC) placed Soná and Mariato districts in Veraguas Province and Tonosí district in Los Santos Province under yellow alert due to heavy rainfall. Rain has already caused landslides on roads in Los Santos, threatening already vulnerable populations, including displaced families who continue to require shelter and basic services. As of 20 October, some 5,000 people remain in 126 temporary shelters, mostly in Veraguas, while others are still sleeping in tents for fear of aftershocks. The earthquake has affected more than 35,000 people and damaged over 9,000 homes, and schools in Los Santos, Herrera, Coclé and Veraguas remain closed. Health authorities are monitoring 908 respiratory and 473 enteric cases as the rain increases the risk of disease outbreaks.

CENTRAL AMERICA: FOOD INSECURITY

El Niño is deepening hunger in Central America’s Dry Corridor, where prolonged drought has left farming families with failed harvests and dwindling food stocks. In the Trifinio border region shared by El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras, some areas have gone up to 75 days without rain. The drought has destroyed much of the Primera maize and bean crop that households depend on to restock their grain reserves. Rising costs are adding to the losses; diesel prices in Guatemala nearly doubled between January and September. An updated Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) analysis now projects that 183,000 people will face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse between November and March 2027, more than double the previous forecast. Guatemala’s Ch’orti’ microregion and Ocotepeque in Honduras are the worst affected.

item.title: Central African Republic: Overview of incidents affecting humanitarian workers (September 2026)
item.description:
Country: Central African Republic
Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Please refer to the attached file.

Since January 2026, 84 incidents have affected humanitarian workers in Central African Republic.
In September, 14 incidents were reported, compared to six in August, an increase of 133 per cent.
This increase may be related to the expansion of humanitarian activities in areas with the presence
of armed groups, as well as administrative restrictions. Despite mitigations measures, humanitarian
personnel continue to be exposed to security incidents in high-risk areas. .
Out of 14 incidents recorded in September, the majority (nine) were criminals in nature, including six
cases of theft and three robberies. Four incidents involved harassment and interference affecting
humanitarian movements, while one incident involved violence during road travel.
International NGOS were most affected organizations, with six incidents recorded, followed by
United Nations agencies with five incidents and national NGO with three incidents.
Since January 2026, the Vakaga prefecture has remained the most affected with 20 incidents
recorded, followed by Bangui with 17 incidents and Haut-Mbomou with 16 incidents.

item.title: CAR: République centrafricaine : Aperçu des incidents ayant affecté les travailleurs humanitaires (septembre2026)
item.description:
Country: Central African Republic
Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Please refer to the attached file.

Depuis janvier 2026, 84 incidents ont affecté les travailleurs humanitaires en République
centrafricaine. En septembre, 14 incidents ont été signalés, contre six en août, soit une
augmentation de 133 %. Cette hausse pourrait être liée à l’augmentation des activités
humanitaires dans des zones touchées par la présence de groupes armés, ainsi qu’aux
restrictions administratives. Malgré les mesures d’atténuation mises en place, personnel
humanitaire demeure exposé à des incidents de sécurité dans les zones à haut risque.
Parmi les 14 incidents enregistrés en septembre, la majorité (neuf incidents) était de
nature criminelle, dont six cas de vol et trois braquages. Quatre incidents concernaient
des actes de harcèlement et d’entrave aux mouvements humanitaires, tandis qu’un
incident impliquait des violences lors d’un déplacement par voie routière.
Les ONG internationales ont été les plus touchées, avec six incidents enregistrés, suivies
des agences des Nations Unies (cinq incidents) et des ONG nationales (trois incidents).
Depuis janvier 2026, la préfecture de la Vakaga demeure la plus affectée avec 20
incidents recensés, suivie de Bangui (17 incidents) et du Haut-Mbomou (16 incidents).

item.title: Panama: WFP Panamá Informe Externo de Situación sobre la Emergencia por Terremoto (21 de octubre de 2026)
item.description:
Country: Panama
Source: World Food Programme

Please refer to the attached file.

ASPECTOS DESTACADOS

• A solicitud del Gobierno de Panamá, WFP comenzó a responder a las 24 horas después del terremoto. Actualmente, WFP apoya la respuesta nacional, en coordinación con las agencias de las Naciones Unidas y la comunidad humanitaria, mediante infraestructura logística, conectividad de emergencia, asistencia técnica y servicios comunes para las instituciones nacionales y los socios humanitarios.

• Hasta la fecha, WFP ha desplegado cuatro unidades móviles de almacenamiento en las zonas afectadas, junto con equipos logísticos, de energía y de conectividad adicionales, contribuyendo a reforzar la capacidad sanitaria temporal, el almacenamiento humanitario, los albergues y las operaciones de respuesta.

• WFP elaboró un marco de respuesta de emergencia de seis meses para mantener los servicios logísticos y de telecomunicaciones y, potencialmente, complementar la asistencia alimentaria del Gobierno. Nuevas evaluaciones y solicitudes gubernamentales determinarán la escala, la focalización y la modalidad de respuesta adecuada.

PANORAMA DE LA SITUACIÓN

• Un potente terremoto de magnitud 7,7 sacudió Panamá el 9 de octubre, con los mayores impactos registrados en las provincias de Los Santos, Herrera, Veraguas y Coclé.

• El Gobierno declaró el estado de emergencia nacional el 10 de octubre y estableció un Comité Interinstitucional de Alto Nivel para coordinar la respuesta, integrado por diversos ministerios y el Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil (SINAPROC), a través de su Centro de Operaciones de Emergencias (COE).

• Las evaluaciones continúan. Hasta la fecha, se ha reportado una persona fallecida y 27 heridas; al menos 35.065 personas afectadas y 5.628 en 126 albergues, sobre todo en Veraguas y Los Santos. Más de 4.000 viviendas, 619 escuelas y 120 centros de salud se han visto afectados. Las lluvias, los deslizamientos de tierra y la crecida de los ríos limitan el acceso a comunidades aisladas y empeoran las carencias de agua y saneamiento.

• WFP visitó las zonas más afectadas como parte de una evaluación interagencial inicial. La misión constató que los mercados se están recuperando gradualmente, aunque su funcionamiento sigue siendo más limitado en las comunidades rurales pequeñas y las zonas de difícil acceso, por lo que se requieren evaluaciones adicionales.

item.title: Colombia | Sitrep 2: seguimiento de la respuesta sectorial en agua, saneamiento e higiene al sismo del 10 de agosto de 2026
item.description:
Country: Colombia
Sources: iMMAP Inc., UN Children's Fund, UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, WASH Cluster

Please refer to the attached Infographic.

Actualización al 22 de octubre de 2026 | Alcance de la respuesta, necesidades humanitarias persistentes y riesgos de desabastecimiento de agua.

El segundo informe de situación (SITREP 2) de la respuesta sectorial en agua, saneamiento e higiene (WASH) al sismo de magnitud 7,4 Mw, ocurrido el 10 de agosto de 2026 con epicentro en San José del Palmar, Chocó, presenta un panorama actualizado de la respuesta humanitaria reportada con corte al 22 de octubre de 2026 en los departamentos de Valle del Cauca, Chocó, Risaralda, Caldas y Quindío. En estos territorios, 29 organizaciones humanitarias reportaron acciones de asistencia en 52 municipios, con un alcance acumulado de cerca de 166.000 registros de personas atendidas. El informe caracteriza la distribución territorial de la respuesta y los tipos de asistencia desplegados, como insumo para el seguimiento sectorial y la identificación de brechas de atención.

Además de caracterizar la respuesta, en el informe se examina las necesidades humanitarias persistentes y las brechas de atención en municipios que ya presentaban privaciones sectoriales previas al sismo. También se identifica territorios donde las afectaciones en los sistemas de abastecimiento de agua coinciden con riesgos de desabastecimiento asociados a lluvias por debajo de lo normal y la posible intensificación del Fénomeno de El Niño, con el fin de orientar la priorización de acciones complementarias de respuesta y recuperación temprana, en articulación con los entes territoriales y la entidades rectoras del sector, prestando especial atención a los municipios con doble afectación y sin respuesta reportada.

La información busca visibilizar las acciones desarrolladas por las organizaciones socias del Clúster WASH Colombia, contribuir a la coordinación sectorial e identificar brechas en la respuesta humanitaria, como insumos para la priorización de acciones y la toma de decisiones basada en evidencia.

item.title: DR Congo: Multi-Country Ebola Bundibugyo Outbreak Update n°23
item.description:
Countries: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Uganda
Source: International Organization for Migration

Please refer to the attached file.

According to the Ministry of Health of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), as of 18 October 2026, the country had reported 9,552 confirmed cases of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), including 4,602 confirmed deaths, resulting in a case fatality rate of 48.2 per cent. Since the beginning of the outbreak, 66 health zones across 8 provinces have reported at least 1 confirmed case. Ituri remains the epicentre, accounting for 72.9 per cent of cumulative confirmed cases. During the reporting period, transmission remained concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu. On 18 October, 97 new confirmed cases were reported (48 in North Kivu, 42 in Ituri and 7 in Haut-Uélé), compared with 88 on 11 October. A total of 41 deaths were reported, including 30 community deaths, while 20 patients recovered. The national contact follow-up rate stood at 76.9 per cent, down from 81 per cent on 10 October, highlighting continued gaps in contact follow-up in active transmission hotspots. Laboratory testing remained substantial, with 500 samples analyzed on 18 October with a positivity rate of 19.4 per cent, compared with 20.8 per cent on 11 October. The outbreak continues to place considerable pressure on frontline response capacities. Since the beginning of the outbreak, 269 frontline workers have been affected, including 180 in Ituri and 45 in North Kivu. Continued infections among frontline personnel reinforce the importance of sustained infection prevention and control (IPC) measures, availability of appropriate protective equipment and operational readiness across affected areas

In Kenya, four additional BVD cases were confirmed on 17 October, bringing the national cumulative total to seven confirmed cases, including the deceased index case. The additional cases comprised one close relative of the index case and three health-care workers who had provided care to the index case. Importantly, all four cases were already in quarantine when detected. As of 17 October, 128 of 130 listed contacts (98.5%) had been traced and were in quarantine, and the Ministry of Health reported no evidence of community transmission.

Key highlights include:

  • The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reported 9,552 confirmed cases and 4,602 deaths. Transmission remains concentrated in eastern DRC, with 97 new confirmed cases reported on 18 October, primarily in North Kivu and Ituri
  • In Kenya, four additional cases were confirmed among known contacts already in quarantine, bringing the cumulative total to seven confirmed cases. Authorities report no evidence of community transmission at this stage.
  • IOM has supported more than 48.2 million health screenings at points of entry and control across affected and at-risk countries since the beginning of the response
  • Nearly 45 million people through risk communication and community engagement activities.
  • Preparedness and response activities continue across DRC, Uganda, Burundi, Rwanda, South Sudan, and Kenya, while preparedness efforts are ongoing in several neighboring countries to strengthen surveillance, community engagement, operational readiness, and cross-border coordination.
  • Population mobility assessments and flow monitoring continue to guide risk-based interventions along high-risk mobility corridors, border areas, and other mobility-affected settings.

For more information, please consult the report HERE

item.title: World: TransformCare: UN Women’s vision for transforming care systems for equality and shared prosperity
item.description:
Country: World
Source: UN Women

Please refer to the attached file.

TransformCare is UN Women’s global initiative to address the undervaluing and unequal division of care work and improve the lives of women and girls worldwide. It advances a vision of care as central to thriving, sustainable, and just economies, where care is valued as a public good, recognized as skilled and essential work, and understood as the foundation of equality and shared economic prosperity.

The brochure outlines why care is essential yet undervalued and unequal, and how investing in care systems can deliver benefits for women, society, and the economy. It presents TransformCare’s global reach, its three interconnected outcomes, and the pathways to change across governments and intergovernmental institutions, businesses, caregivers, and care recipients. It also presents the initiative’s strategic added value, key results achieved since 2020, and the partnerships that support its work across countries and regions.

item.title: Pakistan Weekly Market Monitor (22 October 2026)
item.description:
Country: Pakistan
Source: World Food Programme

Please refer to the attached files.

  • Staple food (wheat flour, edible oils, and pulses) prices remained 24 percent above pre-Middle East conflict levels, as of 22 October, reflecting a combination of domestic market factors and higher fuel and import costs.
  • Wheat flour prices recorded a slight increase (1.0%) during the week, while overall remained 31 percent above pre-conflict levels.
  • The cost of basic food basket for a six-member household stood at PKR 18,719 per month (USD 67) equivalent to PKR 4,680 per week (USD 16.6) nationwide, excluding lower cost items such as vegetables or spices.
  • Petrol and diesel prices remain 47% and 41% above pre-conflict levels despite a slight decline in prices of petrol (-3.6%) and diesel (-1.7%) this week.
  • Regional energy market volatility and disruptions to key shipping routes continue to exert upward pressure on domestic inflation.
  • Food prices remain elevated despite adequate commodity supplies and stable market availability.

Overview

Concern has recognised expertise in the WASH sector and leads more than twenty WASH programmes or programme components worldwide. Our work spans both hardware interventions, such as water supply systems and sanitation infrastructure, and software interventions, including service management, governance, and hygiene behaviour change. Across both humanitarian and development settings, Concern’s WASH programming is grounded in a commitment to quality, equity, sustainability, and reaching people living in extreme poverty. The organisation’s priorities are aligned with its WASH Strategy 2021–2025, which emphasises sustainable basic services, stronger systems, gender-transformative programming, climate resilience, and capacity strengthening.

item.title: DR Congo: Alors qu’Ebola s’étend à une huitième province en RDC, le PAM renforce son assistance alimentaire et son appui logistique à la réponse
item.description:
Country: Democratic Republic of the Congo
Source: World Food Programme

KINSHASA, République démocratique du Congo – Alors qu’Ebola s’étend à une huitième province de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), les familles touchées peinent de plus en plus à accéder à la nourriture tout en respectant les mesures de traitement et d’isolement. Dans un contexte déjà marqué par les conflits, la faim et de fortes contraintes d’accès, le Programme alimentaire mondial des Nations Unies (PAM) fournit une assistance alimentaire, construit des Centres de traitement Ebola (CTE) et met à disposition des services logistiques, de télécommunications et de transport aérien essentiels pour permettre aux partenaires de santé d’atteindre les communautés touchées.

Aucune famille ne devrait avoir à choisir entre respecter les recommandations sanitaires et trouver de quoi se nourrir. L’assistance alimentaire et nutritionnelle du PAM soutient les patients et leurs familles pendant le traitement ou l’isolement, limite les déplacements nécessaires pour rechercher de la nourriture et permet aux équipes de santé en première ligne de poursuivre leur travail. Les services communs du PAM facilitent également l’acheminement des intervenants et des fournitures essentielles vers des zones où l’insécurité et le mauvais état des routes entravent l’accès.

Le PAM a besoin de 214 millions de dollars américains au cours des six prochains mois pour soutenir les populations les plus vulnérables dans l’est de la RDC, touchées par les conflits et l’épidémie d’Ebola. Un financement rapide et flexible est indispensable pour maintenir l’assistance alimentaire, les vols humanitaires, le transport des fournitures et les infrastructures de traitement, alors que l’épidémie atteint des communautés disposant de services limités et confrontées à d’importants besoins humanitaires.

Voici les dernières informations sur la réponse du PAM à l’épidémie d’Ebola et la situation de la sécurité alimentaire en RDC :

Contexte et état de la sécurité alimentaire

  • Dans les zones touchées par Ebola, près de 3,5 millions de personnes sont confrontées à une insécurité alimentaire aiguë de niveau Crise ou pire (phase 3 ou plus de l’IPC). Parmi les personnes directement touchées par l’épidémie, 97 % ont encore besoin d’une assistance alimentaire.
  • Ebola perturbe les marchés, les moyens d’existence et les déplacements, réduisant l’accès à la nourriture alors que les familles respectent les mesures de traitement et d’isolement.
  • Les conflits et les déplacements de population ont laissé de nombreuses familles avec une capacité limitée à faire face à ce choc supplémentaire.
  • L’assistance alimentaire permet de répondre aux besoins immédiats sans que les familles aient à quitter les centres de traitement ou les lieux d’isolement pour chercher de la nourriture.
  • Une assistance prévisible et un engagement communautaire soutenu contribuent à renforcer la confiance dans un contexte marqué par la désinformation, l’insécurité et la méfiance. Les déficits de financement mettent ces efforts en péril.

Opérations et réponse du PAM

  • Le PAM a fourni plus de 744 000 repas chauds dans 59 centres de traitement et d’isolement, ainsi que plus de 3 000 tonnes de vivres aux familles des patients, afin de les soutenir pendant le traitement, l’isolement et la convalescence.
  • Au cours des six prochains mois, le PAM prévoit de distribuer des rations alimentaires sèches à plus d’un demi-million de proches de patients et de cas suspects, afin de garantir leur accès à la nourriture pendant le traitement ou l’isolement.
  • Le Cluster Logistique et Télécommunications, dirigé par le PAM, a mis en place deux bases logistiques, dont une base avancée à Isiro, ainsi que neuf mini-bases en Ituri et au Haut-Uélé, afin de soutenir le stockage, la manutention et la livraison du dernier kilomètre pour l’ensemble de la réponse.
  • Depuis le début de la réponse, le Service aérien humanitaire des Nations Unies (UNHAS), géré par le PAM, a effectué 1 255 vols, transportant 10 272 intervenants humanitaires et 483 tonnes métriques de fret.
  • À la suite de nouveaux cas suspects, des vols de reconnaissance sont en cours d’organisation pour évaluer l’accès à Bole-Bole (Haut-Uélé), Yakoma (Nord-Ubangi) et Biakato (Ituri).
  • Le Cluster Logistique et Télécommunications a facilité le stockage de 3 417 tonnes métriques de fournitures humanitaires pour 43 organisations partenaires.
  • Le Cluster a contribué à l’acheminement de 2 653 tonnes métriques de fournitures essentielles par voie aérienne et routière, notamment des médicaments et des équipements de protection individuelle.
  • Malgré l’insécurité, les difficultés d’accès et les fortes pluies, le PAM a achevé le premier Centre de traitement Ebola de Musienene en moins de deux mois, de la demande initiale à sa remise opérationnelle.
  • Les ingénieurs du PAM continuent de concevoir et de construire des centres de traitement pour le Gouvernement, l’Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS) et les partenaires médicaux. Un autre centre est en cours de construction à Bunia.
  • Quatre autres Centres de traitement Ebola, dont un à Goma, sont prévus mais ne sont pas encore opérationnels.

Besoins de financement et contraintes opérationnelles

  • La propagation d’Ebola accroît la pression sur les capacités de traitement et augmente les besoins en transport, en approvisionnement et en infrastructures médicales.
  • L’insécurité, le mauvais état des routes et les capacités locales limitées ralentissent l’accès humanitaire et les livraisons. Des conditions météorologiques défavorables ont également perturbé les opérations de l’UNHAS, notamment autour de Mahagi, Bunia et Isiro.
  • Le PAM a besoin de 214 millions de dollars américains pour financer, pendant six mois, sa réponse d’urgence dans l’est de la RDC, notamment l’assistance alimentaire vitale, les opérations logistiques et les services aériens humanitaires de l’UNHAS.
  • Sur ce montant, 78,6 millions de dollars américains sont nécessaires pour fournir des repas chauds et des rations alimentaires sèches aux personnes directement touchées par Ebola et à leurs familles.
  • Ce financement permettra également de maintenir les services essentiels de logistique et de télécommunications, les opérations aériennes de l’UNHAS ainsi que la construction de Centres de traitement Ebola.
  • Sans un financement rapide et flexible, l’assistance alimentaire, le transport des intervenants humanitaires et des marchandises, ainsi que l’appui aux infrastructures de traitement, risquent d’être interrompus.
  • Le maintien de ces opérations est essentiel pour soutenir les familles touchées et aider les partenaires de santé à contenir l’épidémie.

Le Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM) des Nations Unies est la plus grande organisation humanitaire au monde. Il sauve des vies dans les situations d’urgence et utilise l’assistance alimentaire pour ouvrir la voie à la paix, à la stabilité et à la prospérité des populations qui se relèvent des conflits, des catastrophes et des effets des phénomènes météorologiques extrêmes.

item.title: WFP Panama: External Situation Report on Earthquake Emergency (21 October 2026)
item.description:
Country: Panama
Source: World Food Programme

Please refer to the attached file.

KEY HIGHLIGHTS

• At the request of the Government of Panama, WFP started responding within 24 hours of the earthquake. WFP is currently supporting the national response, in coordination with UN agencies and the humanitarian community, through logistics infrastructure, emergency connectivity, technical assistance and common services for national institutions and humanitarian partners.

• To date, WFP has deployed four Mobile Storage Units (MSUs) to affected areas, alongside additional logistics, power and connectivity equipment, helping strengthen temporary health capacity, humanitarian storage, shelter, and response operations.

• WFP developed a six-month emergency response framework to sustain logistics and telecommunications services and potentially complement Government food assistance. Further assessments and Government requests will inform the scale, targeting and appropriate response modality.

SITUATION OVERVIEW

• A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Panama on 9 October, with the strongest impacts reported across Los Santos, Herrera, Veraguas, and Coclé provinces.

• The Government declared a national state of emergency on 10 October and established a High-level Inter-Institutional Committee to coordinate the response, including various Ministries and the National Civil Protection System (SINAPROC, for its Spanish acronym) through its Emergency Operations Centre (COE, for its Spanish acronym).

• Assessments are still ongoing, with one fatality and 27 injuries reported to date. At least 35,065 people have been affected, and 5,628 remain in 126 shelters, mainly in Veraguas and Los Santos. Over 4,000 houses, 619 schools, and 120 health facilities have been impacted. Rain, landslides and swollen rivers continue to constrain access to isolated communities and compound water and sanitation gaps.

• WFP visited the areas most affected by the earthquake as part of an initial inter-agency assessment. The mission found that markets are gradually recovering, although functionality remains more limited in smaller rural communities and hard-to-reach areas, requiring further assessments.

item.title: South Sudan — Ebola Preparedness Flow Monitoring Survey — Round 3 (01 – 30 September 2026)
item.description:
Countries: South Sudan, Democratic Republic of the Congo
Source: International Organization for Migration

Please refer to the attached Infographic.

South Sudan (SSD) shares its southern borders with the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Uganda and Kenya, with continuous, high-volume movement that remains largely undocumented at community level. Ebola transmission continues in the DRC following the outbreak in May 2026, and Kenya confirmed cases in Nairobi in October linked to travel from the DRC through Uganda. To inform preparedness along these routes, the third round of the Flow Monitoring Survey includes an Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) module examining travellers’ awareness, knowledge of where to report suspected cases and intended sources of care if they became ill.

Key Findings

Entries exceeded exits at six of the eight flow monitoring points (FMPs). Movement was concentrated at a few points. Nimule Border alone recorded 54 per cent of all counted movements; together with Juba International Airport and Jale it accounted for 85 per cent

The route network centred on Juba, which was the destination for 68 per cent of inflow respondents and the departure county for 73 per cent of outflow respondents

Along the route to DRC, nearly all respondents had reported awareness of Ebola (99%), had received prevention information in the previous month (97%) and knew where to report a suspected case (98%), with health centres reported most commonly as the most trusted sources of information (70%)

Cross-border movement connected the monitored points with areas affected by Ebola. Along the DRC route, 96 per cent of inflow respondents had departed from Dungu and 97 per cent of outflow respondents were heading there, following the reported expansion of the outbreak to Dungu health zone.

item.title: Uganda: East, Horn, and Southern Africa — Transhumance Tracking Tool — Parts of the Karamoja Cluster (IGAD Cluster 1) October 2026
item.description:
Countries: Uganda, Kenya
Source: International Organization for Migration

Please refer to the attached Infographic.

Cross-border mobility of people and livestock remains a critical adaptive strategy across the East and Horn of Africa, notably in arid and semi-arid lands where pastoral communities’ transboundary movement is common. In the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) Protocol on Transhumance it is underscored that pastoralism is essential for safeguarding and increasing production and productivity of livestock and crops in response to climate change, variability and the pressure on existing resources.

The pilot study highlights that transhumance remains a mainstay to livelihoods across the Kenya–Uganda border in the Karamoja cluster. Seasonal transhumant movements are primarily driven by the search for pasture and water, with climate change increasingly altering migration patterns and driving earlier or later than usual movements. Cross-border mobility is common across the cluster, supported by traditional and government resource-sharing agreements, yet challenged by disease outbreaks, limited veterinary services, and mounting pressure on water resources. Early warning systems rooted in traditional indicators remain vital, but tensions at waterpoints and deteriorating livestock health underscore the fragility of pastoral systems. The Transhumance Tracking Tool (TTT) emerges as a valuable innovation, offering data-driven insights to guide conflict mitigation, resource management, and climate adaptation strategies.

Key Findings:

Forty-one per cent of the herding groups moved mainly during the dry season (December–March and July–September) seeking pasture and water. Other transhumant movements were during both dry and wet (29%) seasons, followed by movements recorded only in the wet season (26%) (April–June and October–November) and no regular seasonal pattern (4%).

Attributed to climate change impact, 58 per cent of the herding groups moved in search of pasture and water either earlier or later than usual time of the year. This contributes to 59 per cent of the cross-border movements.

The majority (89%) of the herding groups who move across the borders of Kenya and Uganda in parts of the Karamoja cluster cited search for water and pasture during dry season as driver of transhumant movements.

item.title: Yemen — Flow Monitoring Registry (FMR) Quarterly Report (July - September 2026)
item.description:
Countries: Yemen, Djibouti, Ethiopia, Oman, Somalia
Source: International Organization for Migration

Please refer to the attached Infographic.

This report presents findings from the International Organization for Migration’s (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) on migrant movements to and from Yemen between 1 July and 30 September 2026. During the reporting period, 41,560 migrant movements were recorded across monitored locations, comprising 36,925 arrivals and 4,635 departures. Most incoming migrants were Ethiopian nationals, and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia remained their main intended destination.

The report examines migration trends, routes, demographic profiles, intended destinations, migration drivers and identified vulnerabilities. It also highlights disruptions to maritime movements and monitoring access along Yemen’s West Coast during September, which may have affected the recording of arrivals. Separately, 3,793 Yemeni arrivals were reported in Djibouti between 10 and 28 September amid the escalation of conflict. These arrivals are not included in the quarterly migrant outflow figures
